pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: alt-syscall: add sysctl entry to allow dev mode-only syscalls Chromium OS defines a few alt-syscall tables to whitelist certain system calls in a container. There are scenarios when we would like to expose more system calls to a container, but only do so when the host system is in the developer mode. To allow that, this CL adds a sysctl entry 'kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls', which can be controlled by a privileged system service. The system service decides whether developer mode-only system calls are allowed by performing checks on the current mode and any applied device policies (see CL:421087 and CL:425454) BUG=b:33450588 TEST=Verify that the added sysctl entry '/proc/sys/kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls' exists and can only be written by root. Change-Id: Id7c61b8c13de22c5b0f70b3ebb165e35418d28a2 Signed-off-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/425861 Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: alt-syscall: whitelist perf_event_open for Android Android provides a native profiling tool called simpleperf, which uses the perf_event_open system call exposed by the Linux kernel. Android CTS has a CtsSimpleperfTestCases module that tests various simpleperf usage. To allow simpleperf and CtsSimpleperfTestCases running under the Android container on ChromeOS, this CL whitelists the perf_event_open system call in the alt-syscall table for Android only when we allow developer mode-only system calls, which is controlled by the `kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls` sysctl entry. BUG=b:33450588 TEST=Tested the following on samus-cheets: - Set /proc/fs/kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls to 1, verify that all CtsSimpleperfTestCases tests pass. - Set /proc/fs/kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls to 0, verify that those CtsSimpleperfTestCases tests calling perf_event_open fail. Change-Id: Ie94e85f4b48fce4886597f0e49a125b94b36ca18 Signed-off-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/421087 Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>

login: allow dev-mode only syscalls in containers under dev-mode The alt-syscall kernel module exposes a sysctl entry `/proc/sys/kernel/chromiumos/alt_syscall/allow_devmode_syscalls` for controlling whether certain system calls, which are marked as developer mode only, should be whitelisted for containers. This CL modifies the ui-pre-start job to update that sysctl entry, when exists, under developer mode. BUG=b:33450588 CQ-DEPEND=CL:421087 CQ-DEPEND=CL:425861 TEST=Tested the following: - On samus-cheets (kernel 3.14): * Under developer mode, sign in a registered user, verify that all CtsSimpleperfTestCases tests pass. * Under verified mode, sign in a registered user, verify that those CtsSimpleperfTestCases tests calling perf_event_open fail. - On a system with kernel 3.8, verify that the ui-pre-start job works in absence of the alt-syscall kernel module. Change-Id: I15c432e00ac8a2ac4797817cd5114473c1ce19fc Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/425454 Commit-Ready: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org>

sys-apps/hwids: Add use flag 'hwdb-lite' to reduce hwdb size With our current udev-208 the hwdb information from this package isn't actually included in the binary database /etc/udev/hwdb.bin. This changes with udev-225 and the file now occupies 6+ MB of storage. Some larger items like PCI/USB vendor and model information or OUI isn't really needed on CrOS. Add the new use flag 'hwdb-lite' which excludes some informations from hwdb. The flag is enabled by default. BUG=chromium:676528 TEST=emerge-gru hwids equery-gru f hwids | grep 20-usb-vendor-model.hwdb => no match USE="-hwids-lite" emerge-gru hwids equery-gru f hwids | grep 20-usb-vendor-model.hwdb => /lib/udev/hwdb.d/20-usb-vendor-model.hwdb Change-Id: I1ab405b952d4251028422e7f8458c5bcc9e40e67 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/423195 Commit-Ready: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Tested-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

audiofuntest: close pipe in parent process audiofuntest shares pipes/FIFOs with child processes aplay and arecord. When child process ends, the pipe is still opened by parent process and causes corrsponding read()/write() in parent blocks forever. Close the fds after fork to prevent this problem. Also fixed a nit in help message. BUG=None TEST=Run audiofuntest with another aplay process in background to make audiofuntest fail, make sure audiofuntest is stopped. Change-Id: I67e4d0040ed5ac1239e40d87dae7920101a710e6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/425497 Commit-Ready: Ting Shen <phoenixshen@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ting Shen <phoenixshen@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shun-Hsing Ou <shunhsingou@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: proc: actually make proc_fd_permission() thread-friendly The commit 96d0df79f264 ("proc: make proc_fd_permission() thread-friendly") fixed the access to /proc/self/fd from sub-threads, but introduced another problem: a sub-thread can't access /proc/<tid>/fd/ or /proc/thread-self/fd if generic_permission() fails. Change proc_fd_permission() to check same_thread_group(pid_task(), current).
